title: Every wallet turns on one light
dek: The First 100 Signal turns Network El Segundo's verified-wallet count into a living public artwork
body:
Network El Segundo now has a public signal made by its participants. The field contains one hundred light positions. Each unique Tezos Mainnet wallet verified through the free Kukai message flow turns on one light, and the artwork refreshes from the deduplicated public count every thirty seconds.

The composition publishes collective proof without publishing wallet addresses. It receives only the verified count—no addresses, emails, profiles, page-view estimates, or visitor identifiers. The count remains independently inspectable through the public participant API.

PointCast is carrying the work through the canonical Signal desk, this Block, JSON and RSS feeds, Press Wire, the sitewide first-100 strip, and three contextual house ads. Joining costs zero tez and requires no purchase or transaction. Sale settlement, participant payouts, tokens, yield, and returns remain inactive prototypes.
